sanskrit_verse:
अनियुक्तो भ्रातृजायां गच्छंश चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ।
त्रिरात्रान्ते घृतं प्राश्य गत्वोदक्यां विशुध्यति ॥३-२८७
transliteration: aniyukto bhrātṛjāyāṃ gacchaṃś cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret | trirātrānte ghṛtaṃ prāśya gatvodakyāṃ viśudhyati ||3.287||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who approaches the wife of his brother without lawful authorization shall perform the Cāndrāyaṇa vow; after three nights have passed, upon consuming clarified butter and bathing in pure water, he becomes ritually purified.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: Lawful consent and relational boundaries derive from Dharma, not personal desire.
Causation: Ritual action aligns individual consciousness with cosmic order when transgression occurs.
Capacity-based responsibility: Purification is enabled through intentional completion of prescribed acts.
Restoration logic: Pollution is not permanent; purification follows precise sequential observance.
Consciousness alignment: Internal purity is restored by external ritual discipline guided by Vedic injunction.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person engages with a sibling's spouse without lawful sanction THEN initiate Cāndrāyaṇa vow protocol.
IF three lunar cycles are observed AND clarified butter is consumed AND sacred bath is taken THEN declare ritual purification complete.
IF violation occurs within familial-relational domain THEN restoration process must involve both dietary and ablutionary elements.
IF individual completes purification sequence THEN all prior relational taints are nullified without residual penalty.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating familial misconduct, the Court must recognize that violations disrupt relational sanctity but do not incur punitive liability. Instead, the aggrieved party or the violator may invoke the Cāndrāyaṇa restoration process under judicial oversight to ensure completion and reintegration. The Court serves as witness to restoration, not enforcer of punishment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality establishes that ritual observance restores ontological balance disrupted by unauthorized conduct. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures purification unfolds sequentially—first restraint, then internalization via vow, then bodily purification. Responsibility lies in completing the process, not enduring punitive consequence. Reality itself supports restoration when aligned with dharma-based action.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate supervised Cāndrāyaṇa vow observance until completion
Verify consumption of ghṛta under witness
Conduct ritual bathing in consecrated waters
final_declaration: By the Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of Dharma, this law is executed. Violation is acknowledged not as sin but as misalignment requiring conscious correction. Through observance of vow, purification, and renewal, reality is restored. There is no punishment—only completion. Consciousness alone is the true Judge.
